title: Beldesk Week 3

slides.title: Beldesk — Week 3
slides.label: Opening
slides.notes: EFE · 10 s. Beldesk helps residents report municipal problems and ask service questions in Turkish and English. This week we added retrieval and source-grounded answers.

slides.title: Eight deliverables, with evidence and open items
slides.label: Week 3 / W3.1–W3.8
slides.notes: EFE · 15 s. Show all eight requirements. Distinguish implemented code and measured experiments from human labels, document approvals and customer interviews still awaiting actual evidence.

slides.title: Documents become evidence before the model answers
slides.label: W3.1 / W3.2 / W3.3
slides.notes: EFE · 20 s. The corpus has source, date/version and access metadata. It is divided by section. Lexical and semantic search feed RRF, then a cross-encoder reranker. Sources are evidence, never system instructions.

slides.title: A service answer must point to its source
slides.label: What we built / recorded demo
slides.notes: EFE · 40 s. This is a recorded real run, not a live API call. Read the citizen question, show the answer and its numbered citation, then identify the source sentence that supports it. The municipality and requirements are synthetic.

slides.title: Fixed fallback when no authorized source is supplied
slides.label: W3.4 / software contract demonstration
slides.notes: EFE · 35 s. This is a deterministic software check, not an LLM-generated reply. With an empty authorized-source list the answer module returns the exact fixed fallback without calling the model. Live unavailable-information cases remain affected by the recorded service errors.

slides.title: The denominator is 32, not all 38 questions
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.5
slides.notes: EFE · 20 s. Retrieval metrics use the 32 answerable cases, balanced across Turkish and English. Six unavailable-information controls are tracked separately, not counted as retrieval misses. Gold labels point to source evidence and still need human review.

slides.title: 31 of 32 gold passages appear in the first five results
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.5
slides.notes: DORUK · 25 s. I will explain retrieval quality. Hit at five is 31 of 32, about 0.969. MRR at ten is 0.953. These measure finding sources, not whether a generated answer is correct or faithful.

slides.title: Two ablations: keep the other settings fixed
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.7
slides.notes: DORUK · 25 s. First compare dense and hybrid with the same reranker: the measured quality is equal. Then switch only the reranker off: MRR falls from 0.953 to 0.805. We report both the gain and the absence of a hybrid gain.

slides.title: The same scoreboard; unmeasured values stay null
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3
slides.notes: DORUK · 30 s. Keep the thirteen-row scoreboard used in Week two. Read only measured values. Retrieval is newly measured; task success and repeated agent reliability remain for later weeks. Different test sets and system capabilities prevent a direct Week-two accuracy comparison.

slides.title: Claim-by-claim source support
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.6
slides.notes: DORUK · 20 s. We evaluate claims against actual cited evidence. A citation existing does not mean it supports the claim. Unsupported claims have a clear denominator; missing extraction or judge errors cannot become successful answers.

slides.title: Privacy evidence missed the candidate pool
slides.label: Failure analysis / retrieval
slides.notes: DORUK · 25 s. The English privacy question is the retrieval miss. Its gold passage is outside the twenty-candidate pool, so the reranker cannot recover it. This is a retrieval problem, distinct from a hallucination after finding the right evidence.

slides.title: Retrieval, generation and provider failures
slides.label: Failure analysis / W3.8
slides.notes: DORUK · 15 s. Show an actual recorded case and identify its stage. A missing source is retrieval; an unsupported answer despite available evidence is generation. Do not combine them into one vague error count.

slides.title: The new judge needs its own human check
slides.label: Failure analysis / evaluation
slides.notes: TARIK · 30 s. The Week-three judge checks source support claim by claim and needs calibration against real human labels. We do not reuse Week-two kappa as validation. If labels are missing, we show null rather than invented agreement.

slides.title: A separate judge for source-grounded answers
slides.label: Failure analysis / evaluation
slides.notes: TARIK · 25 s. We preserved Week-two evidence and introduced a separate source-aware evaluation. A contact detail is not automatically fabricated if it appears in an authorized source. A retrieved instruction still cannot override system rules or create a ticket.

slides.title: Human reviews and customer interviews
slides.label: Failure analysis / remaining gaps
slides.notes: TARIK · 25 s. Show actual document approvals, human labels and customer conversations. Any missing work is stated openly. Customer discovery must involve real potential customers; a script or simulated interview is not a completed conversation.

slides.title: Next week: reliable calls and controlled tools
slides.label: Next week / 3 priorities
slides.notes: TARIK · 40 s. Our priorities are to review human-label disagreements and expand the matched sample, measure controlled tool results, and measure multi-step task success. Each priority moves a named metric; retrieval does not itself create or update tickets.

slides.title: Every number should trace back to a command and files
slides.label: Next week / reproducibility
slides.notes: TARIK · 15 s. Commands, source versions and hashes accompany recorded outputs. The final test count comes from the actual test run. The Week-three implementation is shared on its review branch; a release tag and deployment are separate steps.

slides.title: Three questions we expect
slides.label: Questions and feedback
slides.notes: TARIK · 5 s. Thank you. We are ready for your questions.
